title: Fixed pattern bases give no clear median cross-order prediction gain in 53 selected TESS CPVs
abstract: We test whether a few fixed pattern shapes predict changes across Fourier orders in released TESS models of complex periodic variables. We learn shapes in earlier windows and use odd orders in later windows to predict even orders, then exchange the two sets. In 98 visits from 53 selected stars, one learned shape gives a median error reduction of -2.2%, with a 95% star-bootstrap interval of -6.9% to +6.5%. A common depth scale gives -7.1% (-10.2% to -1.6%). Two to four learned shapes give no clear median gain. Controls with shared scale signals give a 12.8% gain at source errors but only 1.2% at twice those errors. The result limits predictive use of these bases in the selected summaries. It does not exclude fixed structures or establish independent clumps. Unknown coefficient covariance, source processing and limited sensitivity prevent a physical rejection. We include original code, aggregate results, a figure, exact input hashes and reproduction steps.
